title: Unit operations (assay2chip stages S2 and S3)
description: The assay rewritten as canonical unit operations (S2), each with the on-chip decision attached (S3). Written to assay2chip/work/<id>/unitops.json; S3 adds `placement` to every op and rewrites the same file. Lab wording is gone by here: every op is something a chip either can or cannot do, and `placement.why` says which and why. Shape defined in assay2chip/README.md.

id.description: The run id, same as the work directory name and as assay.json.

source.description: Carried forward from assay.json so this file can be traced to a document on its own.

placeholder.description: true while this file holds made-up ops rather than real ones.

extraction.description: Carried forward from assay.json, so this file still says which extractor produced the steps underneath it.

audit.description: S2/S3's own provenance: how steps were mapped onto ops, and on what grounds each placement was decided.

ops.description: Canonical operations in process order, numbered from 1. One op is one thing that happens in one place.

op.description: 1, 2, 3 ... in process order. partition.json refers to ops by this number.

from_steps.description: The assay.json step numbers this op covers. Empty only for an op the pipeline added itself (then say so in `note`), because every op should trace back to the source.

kind.description: The canonical operation. load = a one-shot fill of a chamber (merge is a reagent joining a FLOWING stream). culture = long and FED, the only kind that can carry adherent-cell shear. transfer = moving material from one place to another, which S4 turns into a handoff when it crosses chips. If nothing here fits, that is a `missing_part` placement, not a new kind.

confidence.description: How sure this op is, carried forward from the assay steps it came from. Never higher than the least confident of `from_steps`: aggregating steps must not upgrade certainty.

load.description: What the place this op happens in must HOLD. This - not the paper's tube volume - is what S6 sizes a part from. See assay2chip/README.md, 'Bench volumes do not transfer'.

basis.description: adherent_area: cells attached to the floor -> floor area = cells / surface_density. packed_volume: capsules or beads sitting in a bed -> packed volume from count, diameter and the contract packing fraction. suspension_volume: cells or reagent held in suspension at a stated density -> volume = cells / suspension density. flow_through: nothing is held; the part only has to carry a stream (a mixer, a junction, a delay line) and is sized from flow and residence time. none: no load.

cells.description: How many cells (or capsules or beads) the place holds. null when the paper never says - then raise an `unresolved` question and size from a flagged contract default.

surface_density_per_mm2.description: For adherent_area: cells per mm2 of floor, from the paper's seeding density.

area_mm2.description: For adherent_area: the floor area the cells need.

suspension_density_per_ul.description: For suspension_volume: cells (or particles) per uL.

residence_s.description: For flow_through: how long the stream must spend in the part (an incubation in flow, a mixing length).

source.description: paper: stated in the source. derived: computed from stated numbers (say how in `note`). contract_default: the paper never said - a flagged default from contracts/parameters.json, with an `unresolved` question. Never silent.

ratio.description: For a reagent ADDED to a sample (lysis, enzyme, master mix, label): the ratio the paper implies, so the final concentration on chip matches the paper whatever the chamber volume turns out to be. A wash or rinse has no ratio - it becomes a sweep of `-ln(1 - exchange.target_fraction)` chamber volumes.

reagent_to_sample.description: Reagent volume / sample volume, from the paper. null when it cannot be worked out - raise an `unresolved` question.

fluid.description: What is flowing. volume_ul is explicitly null when unknown rather than omitted, so a gap cannot hide.

volume_ul.description: The PAPER'S volume in microlitres, kept for traceability ONLY. It describes a tube, not the chip, and must NEVER size a part: S6 sizes from `load`, S8 sets protocol volumes from the built chamber and `ratio` (assay2chip/README.md, 'Bench volumes do not transfer'). null when the source never said - record it in `unresolved`.

viscosity_class.description: Which fluid model applies. The numeric viscosity is NOT stored here: take it from contracts/parameters.json through assay2chip/lib/contracts.py (fluid.viscosity_37c_pa_s at 37 C, fluid.viscosity_pa_s only for the 20 C dye demo).

particles.description: What is being carried, which sets channel widths, retention and settling.

diameter_um.description: Particle diameter. Required when kind is not none: unswollen diameter, from the source or from contracts (capsule.diameter_um), never invented.

swollen_diameter_um.description: After swelling, when it matters (capsule.diameter_um x capsule.swell_factor).

temp_c.description: Degrees Celsius. null when unknown. Incompatible temperatures are a reason to cut the assay across chips (S4).

shear_class.description: Which shear ceiling applies, and nothing else picks it: adherent_cells -> shear.culture_ceiling_dyn_cm2 (0.01); prelysis_rinse -> shear.prelysis_rinse_ceiling_dyn_cm2 (0.3); capsules -> no shear ceiling at all, bounded by capsule.escape_pressure_kpa x control.pressure_margin instead; none -> unbounded. Read the numbers through assay2chip/lib/contracts.shear_ceiling_for().

placement.description: The on-chip decision (S3). `why` is required on every op: no silent on-chip or off-chip choices.

where.description: pending: S2 has not decided and S3 has not run yet - an explicit 'no decision', so it can never be mistaken for one. S3 MUST replace every pending, and S4 onwards MUST refuse a file that still holds one. on_chip: a block does it. off_chip: it happens on the bench or in an instrument. missing_part: it should be on chip but no block can do it.

part.description: A block id from contracts/blocks.json (basic or advanced, never excluded) - the same vocabulary as every chip spec's `block` field. Required when where is on_chip. S6 sizes it from physics through assay2chip/parts/.

catalogue_part.description: Optional: the chip/components/catalogue.json (Flowmatter) part whose shape this block corresponds to, for display. Reference only - those parts are 1 mm deep and are never placed as-is.

why.description: REQUIRED, always, one sentence: why this op sits where it does. An off-chip decision with no reason is the thing this field exists to stop.

need.description: What part would be required. Required when where is missing_part.

blocks.description: contracts/blocks.json block ids the part is built from, when known.

audit.description: How this op was arrived at: which steps were merged and why, what the numbers were derived from, which contract keys were read.

unresolved.description: REQUIRED, may be empty. Carried forward from assay.json and added to: every value this stage needed and the source never gave. A contract default used in place of a missing number is recorded here with `assumed_from`.

assumed.description: The value used instead, if any.

assumed_from.description: The contract key it came from, e.g. capsule.diameter_um. Never a bare literal.

audit.description: A deliberately OPEN object for the writing stage's working: every other field here is closed, but provenance must never be blocked by a schema. Nothing downstream may depend on its shape.

llm.description: Which language-model mode produced this file (assay2chip/lib/llm.py fills it in).

mode.description: stub means the deterministic offline fallback ran: treat every number as made up.
